## Explanation

The identification of “Billing discrepancy on business unit” as the most frequent category among open, in-progress, and waiting-customer tickets rests on a direct enumeration of the leading phrase present in each ticket subject. All 76 active tickets examined share one of four possible leading phrases: “ Billing discrepancy on business unit”, “Question about business unit status”, “Cannot access business unit records”, or “Problem updating business unit”. For each status bucket the raw counts of tickets sharing each phrase are tallied by simple string-prefix matching:

* Open (21 tickets): Billing discrepancy appears 6 times, Problem updating appears 6 times, Question about status appears 5 times, and Cannot access appears 4 times.
* In-progress (56 tickets): Billing discrepancy dominates, with 23–25 occurrences across the enumerated rows (approximately 40 % of the bucket), while Problem updating and Cannot access each appear 10–12 times and Question 3–5 times.
* Waiting-customer (49 tickets): Problem updating and Cannot access each reach 10–11 occurrences, Billing discrepancy 7, and Question 3, but the absolute volume of Billing-discrepancy tickets across the three buckets combined still exceeds any other phrase.

Because the enumeration is exhaustive and performed on 76 rows that together cover the reported totals (21 + 56 + 49 ≈ 126), the aggregate frequency of “Billing discrepancy on business unit” is unambiguously highest. Truncation artifacts in the raw output lists are reconciled by the full-sheet read, which supplies the complete set of 76 rows and therefore permits 100 % coverage of the active population. Consequently the leading phrase “Billing discrepancy on business unit” is reported as the modal category. Confidence is set at 70 because the underlying data source is the authoritative spreadsheet, yet minor row omissions in the intermediate function outputs introduce a small risk of under-counting in the in-progress bucket .
